relations.subject: n1ql:savepoint
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - a last-write-wins overwrite semantics for a named object. Nothing in the registry expresses this: doesNotSatisfy, isSynonymOf and requiresSetting all miss, and it is a genuine behavioural rule a reader could be surprised by (re-issuing SAVEPOINT s1 silently moves s1 rather than erroring or creating a second savepoint).
relations.evidence: If a savepoint with the same name already exists, the existing savepoint is replaced.

relations.subject: n1ql:multi-statement-request
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted in this batch's transactions.json - fourth occurrence. Server-only.
relations.evidence: If you are using the Query Workbench, you don't need to specify the transaction ID, as long as the statement is part of a multi-statement request. When you start a transaction within a multi-statement request, all statements within the request are assumed to be part of the same transaction until you rollback or commit the transaction.

relations.subject: n1ql:cbq
relations.evidence: Similarly, if you are using the cbq shell, you don't need to specify the transaction ID. Once you have started a transaction, all statements within the cbq shell session are assumed to be part of the same transaction until you rollback or commit the transaction.

relations.subject: n1ql:automatic-transaction-id
relations.evidence: You must be using cbq shell version 2.0 or above to use the automatic transaction ID functionality.

notable_absence.finding: No version, edition, deprecation or access-control statement of any kind, matching the Capella twin exactly. Additionally absent on both products: any limit on the number of savepoints, any statement of whether savepoint names are case-sensitive, and any statement of what happens if you ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT a name that was never set - so the name-collision rule is the only savepoint-lifecycle rule in the docs, and its counterpart (savepoints are destroyed by COMMIT and by a full ROLLBACK) is documented on those two other pages rather than here.

cross_product_finding: This page is one of the batch's four 'near-total rewrites' by line count, but essentially none of the divergence is semantic. The Server page adds exactly the same three access-surface paragraphs seen on every other statement page in this batch (Query REST API requires txid; Query Workbench infers it within a multi-statement request; cbq shell infers it, footnoted with cbq 2.0) plus the cbq footnote. All the remaining diff is the worked-example output being re-rendered from cbq> transcripts into the Query Workbench multi-statement _sequence_num/_sequence_query/_sequence_result response shape, and the Server page annotating four callouts where the Capella page splits the same content into narrated code blocks. SQL++ savepoint semantics - syntax, name-collision replacement, in-transaction-only scope - are identical on both products. Useful negative result for the wave: raw diff size on this tree is dominated by example-rendering and access-surface boilerplate, not by version or edition gating.
version_finding: Nothing beyond the batch-wide availableSince version:cbq-2-0 footnote. Worth recording as a negative: SAVEPOINT is the one statement in this family that has no optional keywords, no synonyms and no settings, so it offers the ontology no version-gating surface at all even in principle.
